paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
coupling_convention: |g^3_aN| isovector axion-nucleon coupling in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis
notes: Paper derives a model-independent 95% CL limit |g3_aN| > 2e-5 GeV^-1 excluded (up to solar trapping bound ~1e-3 GeV^-1) from axion-induced deuteron dissociation using the full SNO dataset. The flat limit of 2e-5 GeV^-1 is stated for sub-MeV axion masses, so I encoded it as a mass-independent bound spanning 1e-22 eV (lowest mass shown in Fig. 1) to 1e6 eV; the exclusion actually extends to ~5.5 MeV with degrading sensitivity near threshold. The constrained quantity is the isovector combination g3_aN=(g_an-g_ap)/2; absent precise cancellation it limits g_an and g_ap individually, so AxionNeutron chosen per the generic-nucleon convention. Emitted values are RAW in GeV^-1 (multiply by m_N~0.939 GeV to obtain dimensionless g_an). The text explicitly states the excluded range: 2e-5 to 1e-3 GeV^-1 for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV, with the upper boundary at 1e-3 GeV^-1 set by solar trapping. The lower boundary is flat at 2e-5 GeV^-1 across the entire mass range (1e-22 eV to ~MeV), rising steeply near the kinematic endpoint ~5.5 MeV (points beyond the 1e6 eV tick follow the text's stated mass reach; the plot extends slightly past the 10^6 tick). Solar axion flux (not DM), so no DM density assumed. The yellow QCD axion band crosses the plot; at m_a~1e-2 eV it sits near g^3_aN ~1e-10 GeV^-1 (calibration approximate).
